---
title: "Peak identification and isotope measurements"
---

![The identification dialog compares a measured peak with isotope candidates.](../assets/tofscope-isotope-identification.png)


Atomic identification searches an offline list of isotope-ion candidates and reports charge, polarity, mass error, and reference provenance. **Identify peak** is beside the mass
spectrum; its plot starts with log intensity. Clicking a peak starts a search immediately; an exact m/z can also be entered. The default absolute tolerance is 0.3 in m/z; changing tolerance, its unit,
or charge and polarity refreshes candidates immediately. By default, candidates have known natural abundances, shown as percentages, and are ordered by abundance within the mass tolerance. Closest-mass ordering and
isotopes without tabulated natural abundance are optional. An isotope can be assigned to an existing signal, an exact window applied to an assigned draft, or a new assigned comparison calculated. The draft keeps its isotope assignment when
you rename it. Original file labels remain unchanged.

**Isotope measurements** sums selected signals at original resolution over the
current ROI and viewing frames, using their common coverage. Fractions are suppressed when windows overlap. Results show percentage shares, a region and frame summary, and explanations for zero intensity or missing isotope assignments.
Calculation details and provenance are expandable. Results describe selected-set
signal ratios, not quantitative composition. Input changes mark
captured measurements out of date until you select **Measure** again. Isotope
CSV and Settings JSON retain scope, mass errors, uncertainties, and provenance;
Save as/reopen also preserves isotope assignments and captured results.
